songs.name: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Ventura set with stellar Truckin' and China Cat > Rider
ai_show_review.blurb: First set rolls through a tight Bertha > Greatest Story Ever Told into a soaring Truckin'. The second set opens with Playin’ In The Band and delivers a rare China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider sequence, followed by a solid Estimated Prophet and The Wheel. Overall the show is high‑energy with strong moments despite some uneven mix issues.
ai_show_review.review: Ventura County Fairgrounds greeted the Dead on a bright July night with an unmistakable spark. The first set kicks off with a punchy Bertha that segues into Greatest Story Ever Told before cruising through fan favorites like They Love Each Other and Tennessee Jed, culminating in a smoking Truckin' that sets a high‑octane tone for the evening. In the second set the band launches into an inspired Playin’ In The Band, then treats the audience to one of the more unusual pairings of the era—a seamless China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider that feels both fresh and familiar. Estimated Prophet stretches out with spacey improvisation, leading into a tight Drums‑Space‑The Wheel sequence that showcases Brent’s lush keyboards and Jerry’s expressive lead work. The set closes with an energetic run through Around & Around and One More Saturday Night before the encore’s gentle “It’s All Over Now Baby Blue.” While several audience recordings capture the sun‑kissed ambience beautifully, the mix can be uneven at times—Phil’s bass occasionally recedes beneath Brent’s synths and Jerry’s guitar may sit low in the mix—but the overall performance remains a vivid snapshot of the band’s 1982 summer groove.

best_recording.reason: Provides the clearest ambience and balances the high‑energy first set with minimal dropouts, making it the most reliable source for this show.

key_highlights: Smoking Truckin' jam that launches the first set into high gear
Rare China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider combo in the second set
Dynamic Playin’ In The Band opener and expansive Estimated Prophet
Clear, ambient audience recording captures the sunny Ventura vibe

band_performance.Jerry: Shows nuanced chord soloing on the I Know You Rider transition and delivers crisp, expressive leads on The Wheel; his vocal phrasing is solid throughout, though some recordings bury his guitar slightly.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a powerful bass foundation that drives the high‑energy jams, but a few mixes note occasional overplaying or a buried low end in certain audience tapes.
band_performance.Bob: Adds raspy vocal color on the Reprise and around sections, and throws in extra melodic ideas during the jams; some recordings feature his guitar prominently.
band_performance.Brent: Keyboard textures are prominent, adding lush pads that lift the improvisations, though at times they dominate the mix over the rhythm section.
band_performance.Mickey: Keeps a steady, propulsive pulse on the drums, complementing Billy’s grooves and supporting the band's exploratory flow.
band_performance.Billy: Delivers tight drum work that underpins the high‑energy set, especially evident during the Truckin' climax and Playin’ In The Band.
